chapter: Hollywood, Ken Murray and the Penguin years
title: Photographs and the sextet winding down
summary: Dresnon neglects bookings and Mosley shifts to a trio.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: What else would you like to have pictures made of, Frank?
The one with Major Eisenhower and with Alberta Hunter. There's one with Alberta. This is also that same band.
Is that the same band? Where is this, Kiwanis Club?
It says something about Greenwich Village.
We were in the village, number one Fifth Avenue.
We got to get to the point where you broke down in the group; how late did you keep the sextet? Jobs started petering out at some point; didn't they?
Dresnon couldn't get you any more work; what was it?
Dresnon was busy, he was a very busy lawyer and he--
He kind of neglected the record business.
He neglected the records and the other business. He had to get a partner to help him out in his law business.

Then we got to a place where I figured it would be advantageous to me in more ways than one that I could make just as much money with the trio and also I'd be able to play more myself. I was criticized for not playing enough in some of my records.
You were emphasizing the show business side a little bit too much.

That's one of the reasons why the records--a lot of the records had not appealed to the jazz people, because of that. They were a little bit too arranged in some cases and there aren't enough solos. The Decca's are probably the best for showing what you can play. The Penguins were too much singing.
